Evos raised $9 million to expand AI software that audits freight invoices, builds loads and follows up on paperwork for small and mid-sized businesses. The New York startup announced the funding Oct. 14 and said its software learns how employees make decisions before doing the work on its own.
What’s Related
Uncork Capital and Field Ventures co-led the round, with participation from Crosslink Capital, Utopia Capital Management, Sandwith Ventures, and angel investors. Evos said the money will fund its growth and the launch of Workhorse, its platform for industrial businesses.
The software is designed for freight , third-party logistics , manufacturing , and other businesses. Tasks include auditing carrier invoices, building loads, following up on paperwork and checking information against a company’s transportation management system .
Evos said it passed $1 million in annual recurring revenue four weeks after going live. That figure reflects annualized recurring revenue, not revenue collected during those four weeks.
Learning the job first
Evos calls its software tools “autonomous operators.” The company says they learn from a team’s behavior, including its decisions and the patterns behind them, and work within the business software a customer already uses.
“The most capable system in many of these businesses is the person who has been there 20 years, and what they know has never been written down,” said Urav Shah, founder and CEO of Evos. “An Evos operator learns the job from these people, improves on it, and proves it can match them before it takes on any work by itself.”
At the start, the company says every decision goes to the customer’s team for approval. A task runs unattended only after the software’s decisions consistently match the team’s, while unfamiliar situations go back to a person.
Each customer receives a model trained only on its own data , Evos said. The software works on top of existing systems without requiring a migration, and the company says customers can go from discovery to deployment in about 24 hours.
A freight invoice audit
At one freight brokerage, an Evos operator checks less-than-truckload carrier invoices against the company’s TMS. Evos said the operator made nearly 3,500 audit decisions over two months.
According to the company, human managers accepted 97.3% of those decisions exactly as proposed. That figure measures how often reviewers agreed with the software’s decisions.
The operator also closed out more than $600,000 in invoice value over five weeks, according to Evos. The company did not report how much the audit saved or recovered in overcharges.

The Hycroft mine is located 90 km west of Winnemucca, and straddles Humboldt and Pershing counties, in Nevada. Credit: Hycroft Mining
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 14, 2026
Hycroft Mining (Nasdaq: HYMC) drilled the highest gold grades yet at its Nevada mine, extending a high-grade zone it’s assessing for underground production.
Hole H26D-6175A cut 19.6 metres grading 30.49 grams gold per tonne and 1,726.72 grams silver from 416.5 metres at Vortex, the company reported on Tuesday. The mine lies about 210 km northeast of Carson City, the state capital.
“The combination of higher grades and longer intercepts suggests we may be getting close to a potential source of the Vortex system,” Executive Chair and CEO Diane Garrett said in the release.
Underground mining could bring richer material into production ahead of a much larger open-pit development, though Hycroft hasn’t established its economics. BMO Capital Markets analyst Brian Quast identified the underground option as potential upside in a Sept. 28 note that estimated a $3.4-billion (C$4.8 billion) construction cost for the broader milling project.
Hycroft’s New York-listed shares dropped 7.2% to $16.30 Wednesday afternoon, after touching $6.48 and $58.73 over the past 12 months. The company has a market capitalization of $1.5 billion.
Narrow core
The latest result includes 1.7 metres grading 347.07 grams gold and 9,526.36 grams silver from 433.2 metres. Hycroft observed visible gold in the core but didn’t report the interval’s true width.
The hole extends high-grade mineralization west and south of previous intercepts. Follow-up drilling is underway, the company said.
Vortex and the neighbouring Brimstone system underpin Hycroft’s underground studies. Their high-grade domains contain measured and indicated resources of 18.1 million tonnes grading 154.71 grams silver and 0.512 gram gold per tonne, for 90.2 million oz. silver and 299,000 oz. gold, according to the January resource estimate.
Hycroft has hired engineering consultancy Respec to develop a conceptual underground mine plan and assess a ramp that could provide drilling access and potentially serve a future mine. Hatch is evaluating processing options, supported by metallurgical testing at Golden, Colo.-based Hazen Research, the company said last month.
The underground concept is to process material into a concentrate for potential sale to third parties. Metal recoveries and concentrate sale options remain under review, according to Hycroft’s September presentation.
Capital demands
Quast removed the speculative designation from his market perform rating and introduced a $24 share-price target in September, citing increased confidence in a restart. His assessment predates the latest drill results.
A decision on restarting heap leaching, which uses a chemical solution to recover metal from stacked material, could be made by year-end, BMO says. Quast estimates $10 million in refurbishment spending in the first half next year and first production in the third quarter.
Hycroft hasn’t committed to that timetable. It continues to assess the restart while testing material suitable for the existing leach facilities, the company said.
For the larger milling project, Quast is modelling construction beginning in 2029 and first production in 2031. He forecasts annual output averaging about 200,000 oz. gold and 6.7 million oz. silver over a 51-year mine life.
His financing model assumes about $2.7 billion in senior secured debt and $1.2 billion in equity. Hycroft held $221 million in cash and no debt at June 30.

BMW overhauled its flagship i7 electric sedan. Now, it wants you to use it as a chauffeur vehicle.
BMW launches i7 chauffeur program in the UK
The 7 Series sits atop BMW’s sedan lineup as its flagship sedan, including its all-electric counterpart, the i7.
As part of BMW’s revamped lineup, which will include 40 new or refreshed models through 2027, BMW introduced the new 7 Series and i7 earlier this year.
The flagship sedan “takes the lead when it comes to the introduction of technologies from the Neue Klasse into existing models,” BMW said.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Unlike the new iX3 and i3, which are ground-up Neue Klasse EVs, the new i7 retains its classic flagship design with a modern twist.
Although it still has BMW’s massive kidney grille, it features a slightly smaller version with available “Kidney Iconic Glow.” It also has a new minimalist crystal headlights that replace the outgoing i7’s stacked headlight design.
Inside, the i7 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and technology with plenty of digital screens. The setup includes a 17.9″ floating center infotainment display, BMW’s Panoramic Vision spanning the dashboard, and a 14.6″ passenger entertainment screen.
It’s powered by the latest BMW Operating System X, which includes an in-car intelligent assistant with Amazon Alexa+ AI technology.
The rear passengers get an upgraded 31.3″ 8K BMW Theatre Screen that drops down from the roof to watch movies or work on the go. Other premium features include new ambient lighting, updated automatic doors, and a digital interior mirror.
To make longer road trips more comfortable, the new i7 features ergonomically designed seats and standard adaptive 2-axle air suspension.
Like the iX3, the new i7 uses BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive. The 113 kWh battery provides up to 447 miles (720 km) of WLTP range. In the US, BMW estimates the 2027 i7 will offer up to 362 miles of EPA range.
Sounds like it would make a good Chauffeur vehicle. BMW UK launched a dedicated Chauffeur Program using the new 7 Series and electric i7.
The program is designed to reduce downtime and help professional chauffeurs grow their business with tailored solutions.
BMW’s program includes Service Inclusive, a five-year service plan covering unlimited mileage for the new 7 Series and i7. It also includes a one-year subscription to BMW Security PRO, a 24/7 vehicle protection and tracking system to safeguard the vehicle.
As part of the program, BMW is also offering Mobility Support, which lets drivers use a licensed replacement or receive support during warranty repairs. It also includes BMW’s high-voltage battery warranty for up to eight years or 100,000 miles.
For those who place an eligible BMW i7 Chauffeur Program order by the end of 2026, BMW is throwing in a free Pod home charger.
The program is available through BMW retailers across the UK and open to licensed private hire operators, chauffeur companies, executive transport providers, luxury hotel house-car fleets, corporate and VIP transport operators, and self-employed chauffeurs. However, BMW said the program is not available to taxi operators.
BMW does not offer a direct Chauffeur program in the US, but the 2027 BMW i7 50 xDrive is now on sale, starting at $106,200. The more powerful i7 60 xDrive starts at $124,700.

Orange is the new green at the University of Tennessee, which deployed a new McNeilus Volterra ZFL electric garbage truck at its Knoxville campus this week, bringing together advanced, battery-electric waste collection technology and Made-in-Tennessee manufacturing.
Campus garbage and recycling routes are a nearly ideal use case for electrification , combining frequent stopping and starting, low operating speeds under heavy loads, significant pedestrian and vehicle traffic, and a noise-sensitive (read: hungover) populace.
To that end, the University of Tennessee chose the Made-in-Tennessee McNeilus Volterra electric platform to reduce tailpipe emissions and diesel fuel use while taking advantage of the truck’s regenerative braking and quiet operation – particularly useful during early-morning collection routes that run by dorms , libraries, and lecture halls.
“The University of Tennessee is an ideal example of how purpose-built electric refuse and recycling collection vehicles can be integrated into demanding, real-world operations,” explains Lee Dreas, president of McNeilus Truck and Manufacturing. “The McNeilus Volterra electric refuse and recycling collection platform was engineered from the ground up to deliver the performance, reliability and operator experience customers expect from their collection vehicles while providing the benefits of an electric platform. We’re especially proud to see a vehicle built by our team in Tennessee put to work at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Vols love their Volterra
By McNeilus Refuse/Garbage Trucks.
“There is something special about putting a truck built by hardworking Tennesseans to work at the University of Tennessee,” said Brad Moats, recycling supervisor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville Facilities Services Department. “The McNeilus Volterra gives us an opportunity to support regional manufacturing while bringing advanced electric vehicle technology directly into our daily campus operations. We’re excited to put this truck to work, measure its performance under real-world conditions and use what we learn to help guide the future of our fleet.”
The truck itself is a Class 8 electric refuse truck fitted with a 499 kWh battery pack (with an optional 665 kWh pack available) sending power through a high-torque e-axle. McNeilus says the Volterra ZFL is designed for all-day operation on a single charge, while published specifications for the platform’s base configuration list up to 110 miles of route capability over a 10-hour shift – more than enough for daily recycling duty around the Knoxville campus.

Ford CEO Tried To Buy a Ferrari Dino at an Auction and Lost
27 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Ford CEO Jim Farley wanted to take a 1972 Ferrari Dino 246 GT home. He stayed in the bidding war until the very end, when someone else offered $1,000 more than he had done a minute before. The reserve was not met, and the car was eventually sold for $76,000 more.
Jim Farley sparked a massive bidding war on Bring a Trailer, trying to take home the classic Ferrari Dino, a stunning model finished in Rosso Chiaro over a Nero leather interior. Farley is a car enthusiast and an avid collector, owning an impressive fleet of rolling treasures.
A 1966 Ford GT40 Mk1 , a 1964 Shelby Cobra 289, and a 1965 Shelby Mustang GT350 are parked in his garage, alongside a 1932 Ford Roadster and a 1987 BMW 325i Convertible. He is also the owner of the most powerful production Mustang ever built, the GTD "Spirit of America." So the Ferrari Dino would have fitted right in.
The auction officially closed with a bid of $366,000 after Jim Farley had placed his most generous offer before it closed: $365,000. The red Ferrari Dino was eventually sold after the auction for $442,000, which far exceeded the highest bid.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Jim Farley has long been an active participant on the collector car auction circuit, bidding on and eventually winning some amazing vehicles over the years. He has also been a seller on the website, where he parted ways with his 1972 DeTomaso Pantera and his 1937 Lincoln Model K Coupe. His yellow Pantera went to someone else’s home for $293,000 after Farley had won the car on the same platform for $121,000 in 2024.
He has also lost several times, admitting last year, in a conversation with Ford Authority, that he isn’t exactly skilled at that particular task. The same publication was the one that saw him involved in the Ferrari Dino auction late last week. It is unknown if he stopped willingly, because bidding went too far or it just ended before he got the chance to make another offer.
A 1972 Ferrari Dino 246 GT arrived in America with a starting price of $13,900, which, adjusted for inflation, would be the equivalent of roughly $85,000 in today's money. Nowadays, the model retails for anything between $350,000 and $450,000, depending on originality, mileage, and condition.
So probably, Jim Farley will be looking for another deal elsewhere, but it won't be easy. Ferrari produced only 2,487 Dino 246 GT coupes and 1,274 Dino 246 GT spyders during the car’s entire production run, between 1969 and 1974. This one rolled off the production line of the Ferrari factory in Maranello, Italy, on May 26, 1972.
Photo: Bring a Trailer So what is Jim Farley actually missing here? The car he lost at auction has spent most of its life, from 1975 to 2023, in California, after being delivered new to Bill Harrah’s Modern Classic Motors of Reno, Nevada. This means that the warm climate protected the gorgeous bodywork, designed by Aldo Brovarone and Leonardo Fioravanti in the Pininfarina atelier, from corrosion.
The Scaglietti-built example has just undergone restoration at Classic Rescue Coachwork LLC of Oakdale, New York, where it was stripped to bare metal and repainted in its original Rosso Chiaro. Prior to repainting, it had the suspension overhauled in 2024 and received an R134a-based air conditioning system in 2025.
The 1972 Ferrari Dino 246 GT is powered by a mid-mounted 2.4-liter V6 engine. Because of strict emissions regulations, the car was tuned differently for North America compared to the rest of the world. While the European-spec Dino came with 192 horsepower (195 horsepower) and 166 pound-feet (226 Newton meters) of torque, the American-spec had to resort to 175 horsepower (177 metric horsepower) and 160 pound-feet (217 Newton meters).
The Ferrari Dinos sold in Europe could rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 6.5 seconds on its way to a top speed of 146 mph (235 kph), but the American Dino was 0.6 seconds slower and maxed out at 142 mph (228 kph).
Photo: Bring a Trailer A five-speed manual transmission with a dog-leg first gear layout puts the power down through the rear wheels. The driver controls the transmission through the exposed chrome gated shifter in the cabin. That is where the fixed-back bucket seats with headrests, upholstered in Nero leather and refurbished earlier this year, welcome the driver and passenger. A Becker Europa II AM/F radio provides the soundtrack on board.
The leather-wrapped steering wheel frames the Veglia Borletti instrument cluster, which includes the tachometer with a redline starting at 7,750 rpm, an analog clock, and auxiliary gauges for oil temperature, coolant temperature, oil pressure, fuel level, and amperage. The five-digit odometer shows this Ferrari has traveled 21,000 miles.
The Dino rides on 14-inch Cromodora five-lug alloy wheels with Dino-branded hub caps and Michelin XWX tires. A full-size spare sits in the front compartment. Four-wheel ventilated disc brakes provide the stopping power. The braking system was overhauled back in 2020. Work involved replacing the hard lines and hoses, servicing the master cylinder, and rebuilding the calipers.
This Ferari Dino got away. Hopefully, Jim Farley will get better luck next time. Fingers crossed for him!
